title: Reply: then oral and written both bound hearers — now only Scripture locks apostolic substance
source_text: XVI. Respondeo, verum est quidem Apostolum, quum haec scriberet, non omnia quae ad doctrinam Evangelii pertinent, scripto tradidisse Thessalonicensibus, sed quaedam tantum viva voce, quaedam etiam scripto, & utraque pari reverentia a Thessalonicensibus suscipi debuisse: siquidem non minor fides Apostolo praedicanti, quam scribenti adhibenda erat. Ultro quoque fatemur fieri posse ut tunc tota Evangelii doctrina, neque ab Apostolo, neque ab aliis scripto mandata esset, quoniam Novi Testamenti Canon nondum constitutus & consummatus erat. Sed inde non sequitur totam Apostolicae praedicationis substantiam scripto postea mandatam non fuisse, tam ab ipso Paulo, quam ab Evangelistis & Apostolis reliquis: aut jam aliquid certi de Apostolica praedicatione posse aliter, quam ex Scriptura sacra haberi. Thessalonicenses quidem, qui Apostolum praesentem viderant & audiverant, de vera Evangelii doctrina certi esse poterant, non tantum ex Scripturae libris qui tum extabant, sed ex viva Apostoli voce quam ipsi perceperant. Sed ex quo Apostoli e vivis excesserunt, de doctrina eorum aliter certi esse non possumus, quam ex eorum scriptis, quibus Spiritus sanctus consignari voluit quicquid necessarium est ad perpetuum Ecclesiae usum. Quae ergo Apostolus partim per sermonem, partim per epistolam, tradiderat Thessalonicensibus, Apostolorum epistolis & Evangeliis postea fuerunt comprehensa, ut, Apostolis amplius viva voce non docentibus, inde salutis doctrina hauriretur. Itaque ex his Apostoli verbis non sequitur ullo modo etiamnum extare certas quasdam traditiones, unde petenda sint quaedam Apostoli praecepta, quae in Scripturis sacris non continentur.
pass_a_gloss: I answer that it is indeed true that the Apostle, when he wrote these things, had not delivered to the Thessalonians in writing all things which pertain to the doctrine of the Gospel, but some only by living voice, some also in writing, and that both ought to have been received by the Thessalonians with equal reverence: since no less faith was to be given to the Apostle preaching than writing. We also freely confess that it could then be that the whole doctrine of the Gospel had not yet been committed to writing either by the Apostle or by others, because the Canon of the New Testament was not yet constituted and completed. But it does not follow from that that the whole substance of the Apostolic preaching was not afterward committed to writing, both by Paul himself and by the Evangelists and the remaining Apostles: or that now anything certain about the Apostolic preaching can be had otherwise than from sacred Scripture. The Thessalonians indeed, who had seen and heard the Apostle present, could be certain of the true doctrine of the Gospel not only from the books of Scripture which then existed, but from the living voice of the Apostle which they themselves had perceived. But from the time the Apostles departed from the living, we cannot otherwise be certain of their doctrine than from their writings, in which the Holy Spirit willed to be consigned whatever is necessary for the perpetual use of the Church. Therefore what the Apostle had delivered to the Thessalonians partly by speech, partly by epistle, was afterward comprehended in the epistles of the Apostles and in the Gospels, so that, the Apostles no longer teaching by living voice, the doctrine of salvation might be drawn from there. Therefore from these words of the Apostle it by no means follows that even now there exist certain traditions from which certain precepts of the Apostle are to be sought which are not contained in the sacred Scriptures.
pass_b_english: True for Thessalonians then: some Gospel by voice, some by letter — equal reverence while Paul preached.
The NT canon was still unfinished — granted.
False now: that apostolic substance stayed unwritten, or that certainty comes outside Scripture.
Hearers then had Paul's living voice; after the Apostles, only their Spirit-sealed writings bind the church's perpetual need — no parallel unwritten precept bank remains.
